title: Grateful Dead Live at Pirates World on 1970-03-24
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT (44.1k) > Sony R500 > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v8.01 Professional > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear matrix recording captures a fire‑filled 3/24/70 set with soaring Dark Star, powerhouse Good Lovin', and a scorching Don't Ease Me In.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers an exceptionally clear and well‑balanced sound (a soundboard‑derived matrix with only a faint hiss) that lets the band’s high energy shine through. Highlights include a cosmic Dark Star, a blistering Good Lovin' jam, a tight Lovelight→Uncle transition and a fiery Don’t Ease Me In, all performed with inspired playing from Jerry and the whole crew. Even with a brief cut at the start of Morning Dew and a splice in Dark Star, the recording remains listenable and exhilarating.

ai_rating.rationale: 20 reviews overwhelmingly 5‑star with only three 4‑star; comments are consistently enthusiastic about both performance and sound quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Balanced SBD‑derived matrix, crisp and clear with a faint 1970 hiss. Minor issues: splice in Dark Star (doesn't affect intensity) and the opening of Morning Dew is cut.

standout_songs: High Time > Dark Star > Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: Festival‑night energy with tight transitions (notably Lovelight into Uncle) and concise, inspired jams. Songs are generally short but packed with fire, giving a fast‑moving yet satisfying flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for scorching leads on Dark Star, High Time, Good Lovin' and the Morning Dew outro; described as 'on fire' and delivering soulful, emotive guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for deep interplay with Jerry—bass sometimes sounds like a separate instrument, adding to the jam texture.
band_member_comments.Bob: His dueling guitar work shines on the Morning Dew segment, providing phenomenal counterpoint to Jerry.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ and vocals are highlighted as commanding, especially during Good Lovin' and Lovelight; his presence adds a vital psychedelic edge.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drumming described as a 'machine‑gun/locomotive' feel with tight solos that complement the jams without overstaying their welcome.
